home.install.title.text: A key, a container, and HTTPS

home.install.snippet.text:
# 1. Generate a master key once, and keep a copy of master.key somewhere safe
test -s master.key || (umask 077 && docker run --rm {image} generate-key > master.key)

# 2. From the folder with master.key, start the server behind your HTTPS proxy
docker run -d --name postkeep -p 127.0.0.1:8080:8080 \
  -v postkeep:/data \
  -e POSTKEEP_PUBLIC_URL=https://mail.example.com \
  -e POSTKEEP_MASTER_KEY="$(cat master.key)" \
  -e POSTKEEP_ALLOWED_EMAILS=alice@example.com \
  {image}

home.install.snippet.compose.text:
# App plus Caddy, which gets the HTTPS certificate for you
git clone {repo}
cd postkeep/deploy/compose
cp -i .env.example .env && chmod 600 .env
# Generate MASTER_KEY once, and keep a copy somewhere safe
docker run --rm {image} generate-key
# edit .env: PUBLIC_URL, MASTER_KEY, ALLOWED_EMAILS, DOMAIN, CLIENT_IP_HEADER
docker compose --profile caddy up -d

home.install.snippet.binary.text:
# Rust 1.94 or newer
cargo build --release
# Generate a master key once, and keep a copy of master.key somewhere safe
test -s master.key || (umask 077 && ./target/release/postkeep generate-key > master.key)

export POSTKEEP_BIND=127.0.0.1:8080
export POSTKEEP_PUBLIC_URL=https://mail.example.com
export POSTKEEP_MASTER_KEY_FILE=$PWD/master.key
export POSTKEEP_ALLOWED_EMAILS=alice@example.com
./target/release/postkeep serve

home.install.needs.text: Back up the master key apart from the data, and keep the same key across restarts and upgrades: it decrypts the saved passwords and sign-ins.

home.works.title.text: The agent apps and mailboxes you already use

home.works.apps.lead.text: postkeep speaks MCP over Streamable HTTP, with OAuth sign-in. Add your server’s /mcp address, and the app opens postkeep’s sign-in page.

home.works.apps[0].how.text: Add a custom connector and paste the address.

home.works.apps[1].how.text: Create an app in developer mode, with the address and OAuth.

home.works.apps[2].how.text: Add a custom connector with the address.

home.works.apps[4].how.text: Run MCP: Add Server, choose HTTP, and paste the address.

home.works.apps.more.text: Other remote MCP clients with OAuth sign-in connect the same way. Clients that only run local servers can use a bridge such as mcp-remote.

home.works.boxes[0].how.text: An app-specific password. The sign-in page shows the steps.

home.works.boxes[1].how.text: An app password, or Sign in with Google. Labels show up as folders.

home.works.boxes[2].how.text: Sign in with Microsoft, with a personal or a work or school account.

home.works.boxes[5].how.text: Added by the server’s operator, with IMAP and SMTP settings.

home.works.boxes.footnote.text: For Outlook, and for Gmail with Sign in with Google, you register one OAuth app with Microsoft or Google. The setup guides walk you through it. Each connection is one mailbox, so add the server to your agent app once for each mailbox you want.

home.tools.lead.text: Plain names, one job each. They work the same way across providers, with a few differences the docs list, such as Gmail sending deleted mail to Trash.

home.tools[0].desc.text: Lists your folders and their roles, such as Inbox, Sent and Trash.

home.tools[1].desc.text: Searches a folder by sender, recipient, subject, text, date, unread or flagged, newest first.

home.tools[2].desc.text: Reads one message: headers, the body as Markdown by default (links and images as references, never loaded) or plain text, and the attachment list with ids; body_format: "text" omits HTML link destinations and images, and body_format: "html" gives the raw HTML when present. It stays unread.

home.tools[3].desc.text: Sends a new plain-text email with any attachments or forwards a message with its attachments. Saves a copy to Sent by default.

home.tools[4].desc.text: Replies, or replies to all, with any attachments, and keeps the thread together.

home.tools[5].desc.text: Marks a message read or unread, flagged or unflagged.

home.tools[6].desc.text: Moves a message to another folder.

home.tools[7].desc.text: Moves a message to the trash, or deletes it for good when you ask.

home.tools[9].desc.text: Shows whether this mailbox’s new-mail webhook is active, paused, off, not set up, unreadable, waiting for a new password, or rules_unreadable (its filter rules can’t be read or compiled), with its outbox limits and filter rule counts.

home.tools[10].desc.text: Turns this mailbox’s new-mail webhook on or off.

home.tools[11].desc.text: Sets how long new-mail events are kept, and how many.

home.tools[12].desc.text: Downloads one attachment of a message: images as images, text as text, other files as base64, or any file as base64 with base64: true, up to 3 MiB. It stays unread.

home.tools[13].desc.text: Lists this mailbox’s webhook filter rules, oldest first, a page at a time.

home.tools[14].desc.text: Adds a rule that chooses which new mail sends an event.

home.tools[15].desc.text: Removes one filter rule, or all of them.

home.tools[16].desc.text: Saves a new draft or threaded reply, with any attachments, to the Drafts folder without sending it. Not available for Outlook or for Gmail with Sign in with Google.

home.tools[17].desc.text: Gives a one-time upload for one file’s bytes, sent with a command, to attach to one message. Off unless the server has a bucket.

home.tools[18].desc.text: Shows this mailbox’s provider, protocol, supported operations, search rules, attachment limits and webhook availability.

home.tools.after.text: You set the webhook address and its secrets yourself, on your server’s account page.

home.selfhost.lead.text: postkeep is one Rust binary, also published as a container image for linux/amd64 and linux/arm64. You choose where it lives and who can use it.

home.selfhost.points[0].text.text: A VPS, a home server, a container platform or Kubernetes. Give it HTTPS, the master key and a volume or PostgreSQL.

home.selfhost.points[1].text.text: SQLite by default. Point it at PostgreSQL and set POSTKEEP_WEBHOOKS=false to run several replicas.

home.selfhost.points[2].text.text: Saved app passwords, Microsoft and Google sign-ins, webhook secrets and filter patterns, stored events and uploaded files, in your bucket, are encrypted with AES-256-GCM under data keys wrapped by a master key you generate.

home.selfhost.points[3].text.text: List the addresses allowed to use your server in POSTKEEP_ALLOWED_EMAILS. postkeep checks it at sign-in and on every request.

home.selfhost.points[4].title.text: An account page for each person

home.selfhost.points[4].text.text: At /account on your server, each person can see their connection, disconnect their agent apps, set up a webhook, or delete what the server keeps about them.

home.mit.title.text: MIT licensed, and yours to change

home.mit.lead.text: Use it, change it and share it, free of charge. The code, the threat model and the October 2026 security reviews are all in the repository.
